The replica-symmetric free
energy for Ising spin glasses with orthogonally invariant couplings
Thanks:

Zhou Fan

Abstract.
We study a variant of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (S-K) spin glass model
with external field, where the random symmetric couplings matrix does not
consist of i.i.d. entries but is instead orthogonally invariant in law. For
sufficiently high temperature, we prove a replica-symmetric formula for the
first-order limit of the model free energy. Our analysis
is an adaptation of a conditional second-moment-method argument previously
introduced by Bolthausen for studying the high-temperature regime of the
S-K model, where one conditions on the iterates of an Approximate Message
Passing (AMP) algorithm for solving the TAP equations for the model
magnetization. We apply this method using a memory-free version of AMP that
is tailored to the orthogonally invariant structure of the model couplings.

Here, we are interested in the more general setting of (

[

[

[

[

an alternative derivation of the TAP equations
using the cavity method and a system of self-consistent equations for the
cavity fields (which we review in Appendix
E

and verified also via a replica calculation that the TAP free
energy evaluated at the model magnetization coincides with the free energy
given by the replica-symmetric formula. At present, few rigorous mathematical
results are known for models with general orthogonally invariant couplings
matrices
J
J
.
Our work is in large part motivated by a renewed interest in
these types of mean-field models in information theory, statistics, and
machine learning
[
50

57
,
48
,
51
,
31

,

,

30

33

53

52
]
,
where orthogonally invariant matrices may serve as more robust models
of regression and sensing designs or more accurate models of
noise in data applications. Indeed, following the initial posting
of this work, several dynamical universality results were obtained in
[
19
,
58
,
20
]
showing that the mean-field dynamics of Approximate Message Passing (AMP)
and other first-order iterative algorithms applied to orthogonally invariant matrices are universal
across broad classes of matrices with delocalized eigenvectors. In many of
these applications, replica predictions for the model free energy
are conjectured, but not rigorously known. Maillard et al. studied in
[
32
]
a class of computational algorithms in the context of
such orthogonally invariant models, extending the diagrammatic expansion
method of
[
46
,
23
,
45
]
to describe the
connections between these algorithms and the predicted mean field
theory; the authors of
[
32
]
highlighted the mathematical
verification of these predictions as an open question.
We study in this work the specific model (
1.1
), and prove
a replica-symmetric formula for the first-order limit of its free
energy in a sufficiently high temperature regime. This extends previous work of
[

This no longer holds when

Our construction of the conditioning sigma-field relies on recent

[

We define

a general class of AMP-type procedures was described in
[

including a “single-step memory” algorithm for solving the TAP equations
that reduces to the one of

in the S-K setting. Our analyses will rely on a

The specific algorithm we use to construct

\mathcal{G}_{t}
is not of the
single-step memory form of
[

40
]
,
but rather an alternative “memory-free” form introduced

[

This memory-free algorithm is related to a class of Vector/Orthogonal AMP
algorithms developed for compressed sensing applications in
[

,

]
, and
may be derived also from the Expectation Propagation
framework of Minka

use of this algorithm leads to two important simplifications:
First, its state evolution has a simple description when

non-Gaussian, whereas that of alternative iterative procedures may
have a complicated dependence on the spectral free cumulants of
J
J
.
Second, the analysis of
[

]
reveals that iterates of this
algorithm have an asymptotic freeness property with respect to
J
J
, which we
describe below in Proposition

. Both simplifications are
important in enabling our computations of the conditional moments in
(

The details of our strategy for showing (

somewhat different from those presented in
[

we proceed in two high-level steps: We first apply the AMP
state evolution and a large deviations argument to give exact expressions for
the large-

in terms of low-dimensional variational problems. This leverages and
extends some results of Guionnet and Maıda
[

relate exponential integrals over the orthogonal group to the R-transform of

. We then analyze these
variational problems, proving upper and lower bounds for their values
that are tight for
Ψ

\Psi_{\mathrm{RS}}
and
2
​
Ψ

2\Psi_{\mathrm{RS}}
in the limit as the number of algorithm iterations

→
∞

. The assumption of small

(i.e. sufficiently high
temperature) is used in a crucial way in the upper bounds, to show a global
concavity property of these variational problems.
The remainder of the paper is organized as follows: In Section

we collect the general ingredients of the proof, including a more detailed

respectively, leading to the proof of Theorem

Instructions for reporting errors
We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile
support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the
methods listed below:
Click the "Report Issue"
(
)
button, located in the page header.
Tip:
You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.
Our team has already identified
the following issues
. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
all.
Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a
list of packages that need conversion
, and welcome
developer contributions
.
